issues.legal_issue: A later suit for possession based on title is not barred by the claim-splitting rule when the earlier suit sought the sale price under an agreement and arose from a different cause of action.
material_facts: The earlier suit sought recovery of the land’s sale price under a document held to be an agreement for sale rather than a sale deed.
The later suit sought possession on the basis that the plaintiffs owned the land.
The plaintiffs could not have sought possession on the basis of title in the earlier suit, where they had alleged that title had been transferred to the defendants.
issues.conclusion: The causes of action in the two suits were different, so the later suit was not barred by Order II Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
issues.legal_principle: Order II Rule 2 requires a plaintiff to include claims and reliefs arising from the same cause of action, but does not bar a later suit founded on a distinct cause of action. The Court relied on Palaniappa Chettiar v. Alagan Chettiar; Arun Lal Gupta v. Mriganka Mohan Sur; State of Madhya Pradesh v. State of Maharashtra; Kewal Singh v. Mt. Lajwanti; Sidramappa v. Rajashetty; and Gurbux Singh v. Bhura Lal. Gurbux Singh states that the party raising the bar must establish identity of causes of action, entitlement to more than one relief in respect of that cause, and omission of the later relief without leave.

rule.if: successive_suits and later_suit_challenged_under_claim_splitting_rule and earlier_suit_sought_sale_price_under_transfer_agreement and later_suit_sought_possession_based_on_title and causes_of_action_are_distinct

predicates.successive_suits: A plaintiff brought a later suit after an earlier suit against the same defendant.
predicates.later_suit_challenged_under_claim_splitt: The defendant contended that the later suit was barred because relief had been omitted from the earlier suit.
predicates.earlier_suit_sought_sale_price_under_tra: The earlier suit sought the price of land under a document treated as an agreement to transfer it.
predicates.later_suit_sought_possession_based_on_ti: The later suit sought possession on the basis of the plaintiff’s ownership of the property.
predicates.causes_of_action_are_distinct: The facts and legal basis giving rise to the later claim differed from those underlying the earlier claim.

issues.definition: When successive suits involve distinct causes of action, the later suit is not barred by the claim-splitting rule even if it seeks relief not sought earlier.

issues.legal_issue: A prior finding on an issue does not establish res judicata in a later suit where the party does not plead preclusion and the issue is not raised or tried in that suit.
material_facts: In the earlier suit, the trial court found that the defendants were tenants, but the appellate court reversed that finding.
In the later possession suit, the defendants did not plead res judicata or claim that they were tenants; they relied instead on adverse possession and other defences.
No issue about whether the defendants were tenants was framed or tried in the later suit.
issues.conclusion: The defendants could not invoke res judicata based on the earlier trial court’s finding because the plea was not raised and the tenancy issue was not raised, framed, or tried in the later suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure bars trial of a matter directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties, litigating under the same title, when it was heard and finally decided by a competent court. The Court explained that the rule is based on finality of litigation and preventing a party from being vexed twice for the same cause; the necessary basis for its application was absent here.

predicates.later_civil_suit_invokes_prior_judgment_: A party in a later civil suit seeks to rely on a determination made in an earlier suit.
predicates.preclusion_not_pleaded_in_later_suit: The party relying on the earlier determination did not plead that the later suit or issue was precluded.
predicates.prior_issue_not_raised_or_tried_in_later: The issue determined earlier was not raised, framed, or tried in the later suit.

issues.definition: Where a party does not plead preclusion and the previously determined issue is not raised or tried in the later suit, the earlier finding does not preclude the later suit on that issue.

issues.legal_issue: A possession decree may be modified in the interests of justice to preserve part of the land for occupants who have remained in possession for a considerable time.
material_facts: The occupants had remained in possession of the land for a considerable time.
In the earlier suit, the owners had alleged that the land had been sold to the occupants and sought the sale price.
The Court considered that the interests of justice would be served by leaving a compact portion of the land with the occupants.
issues.conclusion: The Court modified the possession decree, treating the occupants as protected tenants over a portion of the land and directing that the decree be executed for the remainder, with partition by the Tehsildar.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on its assessment of the interests of justice in light of the occupants’ prolonged possession and the owners’ earlier assertion that the land had been sold to them. It cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this modification.

predicates.appeal_from_possession_decree: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a decree for possession of land.
predicates.occupants_in_long_possession: The persons resisting possession have remained on the land for a considerable time.
predicates.owner_previously_asserted_transfer_to_oc: The party claiming ownership had earlier asserted that the land was transferred to the occupants.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a possession decree, prolonged possession and the owner’s earlier assertion of transfer may lead to preserving part of the land for the occupants as protected tenants.
